- File: scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 2271-2314 (the export/unset block)
  Problem: The `unset GIT_INDEX_FILE` removes the variable entirely from the script's environment after the model attempt. If a caller had set `GIT_INDEX_FILE` before invoking this script (e.g. for some external reason in the source-repo path), that inheritance is lost after the first attempt. In practice `IS_WORKFLOW_SOURCE_REPO=true` only ever fires for this repository in the Actions environment, where no caller sets `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, so this is not a runtime issue.
  Why it fails at runtime: It does not fail at runtime in any documented execution path; the scenario requires an upstream caller to have set the variable, which the workflow does not do. Not a defect.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 1
- File: scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh
  Line or code reference: lines 2217-2226 (the `_resolver_prepare_scratch_index` call after `capture`)
  Problem: The helper does `rm -f` then `cp` of the real index. If the real index does not exist (fresh repo, no commits), `cp` is skipped because of the `[ -f "${real_index}" ]` guard — good. However, the `unset GIT_INDEX_FILE` in the cleanup block runs only when `_resolver_index_isolated=true`. If the script is killed (SIGKILL) between the model exit and the cleanup block, `GIT_INDEX_FILE` remains set in the script's environment but the scratch file is removed by the next attempt's `rm -f` prelude. This is not a defect — `RUNTIME_DIR` is per-run and the next attempt's helper cleans up — but worth noting as a minor leak window.
  Why it fails at runtime: It does not fail; the helper re-seeds on every attempt and the file is in a per-run directory. NIT only.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

- File: docs/plans/issue-4545-resolver-index-isolation-plan.md
  Line or code reference: Approach section, bullet "The model's own `git add`/`git commit` (if it runs one despite the prompt change) writes to the scratch copy only."
  Problem: This newly-added plan doc still claims a model-issued `git commit` "writes to the scratch copy only." AD-2 (recorded in docs/implement-plan/issue-4545-resolver-index-isolation.md) explicitly lists "the plan's Approach" among the docs that said this and whose correction was picked as "correct the comments/docs to say only the index is isolated and a model commit still fails closed." The script comment (scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:646-647), agents.md (lines 1944-1947), and the changelog fragment were all corrected to state that `git commit` still moves HEAD and removes MERGE_HEAD, but the plan's Approach bullet was not. The claim is now inconsistent with the code it describes: `git commit` with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` set writes the index to the scratch copy, but it also moves `HEAD` and removes `.git/MERGEGE_HEAD`, which are not isolated by `GIT_INDEX_FILE` (pinned by `test_scope_isolated_model_commit_still_fails_closed`).
  Why it fails at runtime: No runtime failure — the code and the live docs (agents.md, changelog, script comment) are correct; only the historical plan doc retains the inaccurate statement. A future reader using the plan as the canonical description of the isolation mechanism would misunderstand the containment boundary.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh
  Location: _resolver_prepare_scratch_index (lines 651-658)
  Issue: When IS_WORKFLOW_SOURCE_REPO=true and the workspace safety check fails (_run_codex=false, line 2264-2268), _resolver_prepare_scratch_index has already created the scratch file at line 2220, but the cleanup block at lines 2308-2311 is inside the `if [ "${_run_codex}" = "true" ]` guard and so never runs. The scratch file is left on disk until the next iteration's _resolver_prepare_scratch_index re-seeds it (rm -f then cp). This is harmless (the file is not referenced after the attempt), but cleaning it up on the no-model path would keep RUNTIME_DIR tidy and avoid a stale file surviving a single-attempt run.
  Suggested minimal fix: Add `rm -f "${RESOLVER_SCRATCH_INDEX}"` inside the `_run_codex=false` branch (after line 2268), or move the existing cleanup so it also runs when the safety check skips the model.
  Estimated lines changed: 1
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
